verified_claims: A subsea fiber break severed internet and wireless service to six Aleutian communities: Akutan, Chignik Bay, False Pass, King Cove, Perryville, and Unalaska. (Alaska Public Media June 1 + KUCB May 29, two independent in-window sources)
GCI bridged affected traffic onto satellite backup; basic wireless and limited mobile data were restored by about June 1.
GCI said full fiber repair was expected within roughly one to two weeks of the late-May/June-1 announcements (i.e., mid-June).

softened_or_stripped.claim: Repair vessel on-site near Chignik Bay June 6
softened_or_stripped.reason: No fetched page confirms a June 6 vessel arrival; sources give a 7-14 day repair window from late May / June 1. Use 'expected within one to two weeks' / 'by mid-June'.

softened_or_stripped.claim: Unalaska-Dutch Harbor is the second-busiest fishing port in the nation
softened_or_stripped.reason: Not on any fetched source page. Do not assert any numeric port ranking. May refer to Unalaska as an Aleutian fishing hub generically.

sources.author: Ted Hearn
sources.note: paywalled body; cite only for the framing question, not for specific figures

verified_claims: Alaska telecoms received $4.6 billion in Universal Service Fund subsidies since 2016, more than $600 per Alaskan per year, the most of any state. (ADN + ProPublica, both May 19, independently confirmed)
Alaska's broadband speeds were recently clocked as the slowest in the country.
GCI received $466 million two years after settling fraud allegations in the same program.
The FCC has circulated a proposal to overhaul or sunset the Alaska Plan subsidy mechanism.
GCI is acquiring Quintillion at a $310 million enterprise value, deepening its exposure to Arctic subsea fiber. (GCI newsroom, primary)
GCI holds $121.2 million in BEAD grant obligations to extend fiber to rural Alaska communities. (GCI newsroom, primary)

softened_or_stripped.claim: Specific Jan/Feb 2026 break dates (Unalaska blizzard, Deering)
softened_or_stripped.reason: Paywalled source; characterize generally as repeated subsea breaks over the past year, attributed/reportedly.

verified_claims: DAF is offering roughly 4,700 acres across JBER, Eielson AFB, and Clear SFS for privately financed AI data centers under leases up to 50 years. (Air and Space Forces Magazine)
Proposals were due May 29, 2026; no award or shortlist announced as of June 6. (ADN)
Chugach Electric stated it does not currently have gas to serve a large data center. (ADN, verbatim)

Stak Energy has preliminary state approval to lease North Slope land for a roughly $500 million natural-gas-powered AI/cloud data center, with no investors or customers publicly disclosed. (Alaska Public Media, single non-primary source)
Stak is led by CEO Sparrow Mahoney and has hired former DNR commissioner John Boyle.

softened_or_stripped.claim: 715.4 acres, up to 3GW, 50-year lease, May 12 DNR finding, June 15 comment deadline, Milepost 390
softened_or_stripped.reason: Northern Journal 404, DNR 503; none verified on the one accessible page. Use only $500M, North Slope, preliminary approval, no disclosed investors/customers.

summary: Deep Dive on the GCI Aleutian subsea fiber break (in-window, two independent sources), framed against the verified $4.6B USF-subsidy structure (ADN/ProPublica) and the AI-hosting-frontier pitch (DAF ~4,700-acre lease, Stak $500M North Slope proposal). The position: capital is chasing the top of the AI stack on a connectivity substrate that is both physically fragile and under federal subsidy review.
